headline: New law requires the State Department to review and report to Congress every two years on its rules for dealing with Taiwan.
what_it_does: Before this law, the State Department had to review its guidance on U.S. relations with Taiwan only once and report to Congress. Now it must do that review and report every two years for as long as the guidance is in effect. Each report must explain how the guidance reflects certain factors, such as Congress's view that Taiwan has a government chosen through free and fair elections. Reports must also name chances and plans to lift limits the U.S. has placed on its own dealings with Taiwan.

who_it_affects.how: It must review its Taiwan guidance and send a report to Congress every two years instead of just once.
They will receive regular reports on how federal agencies are told to handle relations with Taiwan.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that work with Taiwan
who_it_affects.how: The guidance they follow on contact with Taiwan will be reviewed regularly and could be changed if restrictions are lifted.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 2, 2025; the summary does not give a specific start date for the first report.
